AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: To identify risk factors associated with the failure of extubation of mechanically ventilated very-low-birth-weight newborns.

AbstractText.Label: STUDY DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Prospective observational study. Assessment of the occurrence of extubation failure in relation to demographic and ventilation parameters, the SpO2/FiO2 ratio, the spontaneous breathing test (SBT) and values of the Silverman-Andersen score (SAS). Extubation failure was defined as the need for reintubation for any reason within 72 h after extubation.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Extubation failed in 14/50 (28%) patients. Tidal volume applied at the moment of extubation (p = 0.030), the values of the SpO2/FiO2 ratio (p = 0.006), SBT (p = 0.034) and SAS measured for 60 min after extubation and later (p = 0.010, p = 0.000001, p∼0.000, respectively) showed a significant association with reintubation.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Measured TV, SpO2/FiO2 ratio, SBT at the moment of extubation and values of SAS starting 1 h after extubation might be valuable parameters in identifying those VLBW newborns in the risk to fail extubation.
